races.name: Matchbook Signup- Get 20% Back On Losses Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Havana Halo
runners_data.note: An OR-62 hold-up filly whose recent form shows a second at this course on good ground, but she is bundled into a midfield slot here because the field is overloaded with closers, and her ability to produce a late run depends entirely on a pace collapse that may not materialise at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked well down our figures among this field, Havana Halo faces a stiff task at 132 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and second last time out shows she can place when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Warrior
runners_data.note: One of two confirmed front-runners who will set the race alight from the gates; a winner over 6f on good ground but with a patchy record in competitive company, and the key question is whether he can absorb Punchbowl Flyer's challenge and stay on rather than folding once headed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Zoulu Warrior does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and twenty days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, though his 131 lb burden from stall six and a mid-table ranking among fourteen rivals reflect the uphill task he faces.

runners_data.name: Lahina Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent 6f performer for Rachel Cook and John Bridger who has been placed in six of her last six attempts on good or standard ground and was second here over course and distance last time; running out of a prominent position suits this race shape ideally, and she arrives only six days since her last run but has shown no bounce issues.

runners_data.name: Yes Waliim
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's three-year-old won over 7f on standard going but is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield by race dynamics; the drop back to 6f on good ground is a query for a horse whose recent win came over further, and the first-time hood (hg:p) may sharpen focus.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the 14 runners on our figures, Yes Waliim faces a stiff ask, and his recent form — largely modest across his last six starts — does little to inspire confidence, though a win two starts back and a runner-up last time out at least show he retains some ability, and he has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Stock Market
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's three-year-old has placed consistently on good and soft ground at sprint trips, wearing a hood (hg:b), and though his natural instinct is to come from off the pace, he finds himself in the thick of a midfield pack that blunts his late kick — the style mismatch caps his ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but a model of consistency, Stock Market has placed three times in that run — third last time out and second four starts back — and has experience of today's distance and going; the weight of 125 lb and stall 12 are the factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Distant Rumble
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old has genuine hold-up credentials with two wins and four placings on good ground over 6f, and his OR of 68 gives him class at the top of this field; needs a genuine pace collapse to be at his best, and with 46 days between runs a blow-out run is possible if he lacks fitness sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Distant Rumble brings distance and going experience to the table, and his win and runner-up placing in recent starts show he can perform at this level; our rating of 76 marks him out as a leading threat, though back-to-back sevenths last time out give the main cause for concern.

runners_data.name: Good Earth
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's nine-year-old is a tough veteran who races prominently and handles good ground at Windsor well, with a recent runner-up at 5f showing he retains ability; the step up to 6f on this track suits his rolling style, and Connor Planas keeps it simple from the front of the chasing pack.
runners_data.comment: Good Earth arrives here on the back of a fourth last time out, and though winless in recent starts, he has experience over today's trip and going, returns fit on a quick turnaround of ten days, and his rating of 74 offers an edge over his official mark of 68.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Knocker
runners_data.note: Andi Brown's five-year-old wears a tongue-tie (hg:t) and has struggled to convert decent placings into wins over Windsor's 6f trip on good ground; the hold-up style is genuine but his record of three wins and two placings in 15 attempts on good ground suggests he needs things to fall perfectly in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Jimmy Knocker showed a spark when second two runs back but has otherwise struggled for consistency, and 137 lb from stall 14 adds to the task, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Come On Eibhlin
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old has abundant good-ground form but her wins and placings have nearly all come at 7f and beyond, making this 6f test on a flat track a stamina question in reverse — she is a hold-up horse who needs the trip to stretch out, and 6f may simply not give her enough time to wind up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Come On Eibhlin nonetheless shaped with promise when third last time out and our rating of 75 marks her as a genuine threat from this field; the concern is that a ninth two starts back hints at inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Noelies Dream
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's second runner has been off the track for 269 days — a major freshness concern — and has only one run on good going in her profile; a winner at 5f on standard, she has no proven form at Windsor or on a flat 6f straight, and the layoff clouds her fitness entirely.
runners_data.comment: Noelies Dream returns from a 269-day absence, which is the dominant concern here, and our rating of 61 leaves him well below the majority of rivals; he has run over today's trip before and his win two starts back offers a shred of encouragement, but he is hard to fancy on these figures.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: Alexandra Egan partners this nine-year-old front-runner who has two wins and two placings from just three runs on good ground over 6f, including back-to-back wins; wearing a hood (hg:b), he is the most likely horse to get to the front alone if Zoulu Warrior's early speed is not as sharp, and course-and-distance winning form makes him the pace anchor of this race.
runners_data.comment: Punchbowl Flyer has shown he can win, landing back-to-back victories three and four starts back, but successive sixth and seventh-place finishes since make him hard to fancy, and a ranking of twelfth of fourteen on our figures only adds to the concern, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Patat
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's nine-year-old has winning and placing form on good ground at sprint trips but his true hold-up style is squeezed into midfield because there is no room at the rear; despite solid handicap credentials, the style displacement means he is unlikely to produce his most effective finish unless the pace is extreme.
runners_data.comment: Monsieur Patat has experience over today's trip and going, and a second three starts back suggests ability, yet he has been winless in his last five outings and finished fifth last time out, making progress from stall five under 134 lb a tall order.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old has back-to-back wins on good ground at 6f and is genuinely well-treated on an OR of 64 given that form, but as a natural hold-up horse he is displaced into midfield against his instincts; Hope Regan takes a 7lb claim and if she can manoeuvre him into a clear run in the straight his late kick is a real threat.
runners_data.comment: Arnaz won two of his last six starts, with back-to-back victories two and three runs back, though he has since finished sixth, making his recent form a touch inconsistent; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 15 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends out this seven-year-old who has placed four times in ten recent runs on good going, wearing a visor (hg:v); he is a hold-up horse shuffled into the midfield pack, and while his course-and-distance placing record shows he can hit the frame, he has not won in a competitive field and is unlikely to dominate from a compromised position.
runners_data.comment: Rebel Path arrives here in decent order after a third two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going gives him every right to feature — our rating has him narrowly top-rated, making the lack of a recent win the one concern to weigh.

runners_data.name: Rory's Royale
runners_data.note: Simon Hodgson's four-year-old returns from 191 days off the track — the longest break in this field — and all five of his recent runs have been over 7f on standard going, so this 6f good-ground Windsor test is a significant change of conditions; wears a visor (hg:v) and is a hold-up horse placed into midfield, meaning he faces unknowns on every front today.
runners_data.comment: Rory's Royale has experience over today's trip and going, and a third four starts back offers some encouragement, but he returns after 191 days off and has been winless in recent starts, with a sixth last time out giving little reason for confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Punchbowl Flyer and Zoulu Warrior are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates on this straight Windsor 6f, creating a genuinely competitive early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested pace. With both committed to making the running, the race will be run at an honest tempo throughout, compressing the advantage available to the pace-setters and leaving the field strung out early. Lahina Bay and Good Earth are best placed to capitalise from a prominent position just off the speed, travelling into a race that suits those who can slot in second or third early and pick up the pieces if the two leaders burn each other off. This race shape most favours prominent racers with tactical flexibility — true hold-up horses face an uphill task because the honest gallop does not generate enough of a pace collapse to create the surge they depend on, and the field holds more hold-up types than the race can physically accommodate at the rear: Monsieur Patat, Arnaz, Rebel Path, Rory's Royale, Havana Halo, Yes Waliim and Stock Market are all genuine hold-up horses who will be shuffled into midfield, with Lahina Bay and Good Earth most likely to secure the advantageous prominent slots behind the two leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Punchbowl Flyer and Zoulu Warrior lock horns early and set a true gallop that leaves the front two vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lahina Bay and Good Earth, sitting close to the pace without burning energy, are ideally positioned to sweep past tired leaders approaching the final furlong, with Lahina Bay's consistent 6f Windsor form giving her a particular edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Punchbowl Flyer Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Zoulu Warrior fails to match Punchbowl Flyer's early stride and concedes the lead, allowing Alexandra Egan to control proceedings at a measured tempo.
scenarios.body: Punchbowl Flyer, a two-time winner on good ground over course and distance, thrives when allowed to dictate on a flat track without a serious challenger, and an uncontested lead dramatically improves her chance of lasting home. Lahina Bay, tracking just off the pace, remains the most dangerous pursuer if the pace proves sustainable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace between Punchbowl Flyer and Zoulu Warrior is truly scorching and produces a significant fade from the front two.
scenarios.body: Distant Rumble has the strongest hold-up credentials in the field with an OR of 68 and a proven record of finishing strongly in 6f handicaps on good ground, and would be the primary beneficiary of a genuine collapse in the leaders; Arnaz has winning form on good going at this trip and, though mapped to midfield against his natural style, has the ability to hit the line hard if able to find daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, No Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war is absolute and the hold-up horses, crammed into midfield, cannot find a clear run in time to deliver a meaningful challenge.
scenarios.body: With so many true closers unable to get their natural position, traffic problems in the straight become a real risk, and a messy finish where no horse can dominate suits a shrewd prominent racer sneaking through the chaos. Good Earth's veteran course savvy over 5f-6f at Windsor makes her capable of exploiting a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Punchbowl Flyer and Zoulu Warrior — watch for an overly aggressive early battle between these two front-runners that could set a suicidal pace and leave both vulnerable to a late challenge from Lahina Bay from the two-furlong pole.

Arnaz — despite being displaced into midfield against his hold-up instincts, two recent wins on good going at 6f with Hope Regan claiming 7lb makes him a horse to monitor if he secures an early clear run on the stands side or centre of the track.

Lahina Bay — returning only six days after her last run and racing prominently; watch whether she takes up her customary prominent pitch cleanly from stall draw, as any early traffic would undermine the key advantage her consistent finishing position provides.

Noelies Dream — 269 days off the track is the standout freshness flag in this field; watch market moves before the off, as any significant support would suggest the yard has done serious home work and she is ready to fire first time back.

Rory's Royale — 191-day absence combined with a switch from 7f standard to 6f good ground and a move to the visor for the first time makes this horse worth monitoring in the early stages to assess how well she is travelling before the halfway mark.

races.name: Hamish Johnson Memorial EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Santo
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly has placed twice at 6f on Good ground and her prominent style maps neatly onto the predicted pace shape — tracking the front-runners and pouncing suits her proven ability to finish off races at this trip.

runners_data.name: Highland Grey
runners_data.note: Ran only over 7f on Soft for Roger Teal so this is a step down in trip and step up in ground speed; hold-up style means she needs the pace to collapse entirely and represents a degree of unknown.

runners_data.name: Pent Up Charm
runners_data.note: Michael Madgwick's filly faded badly on her sole start at 6f Good and the finish-fade flag is a significant concern here given the strong gallop will test stamina, not mask weakness; Isobelle Chalmers' 7lb claim partially offsets the weight burden.

runners_data.name: Romotoso
runners_data.note: William Knight's filly is a confirmed front-runner with Oisin Murphy aboard — a major upgrade in jockey quality — and her placed form over 6f on Good gives her credibility; her ability to control pace rather than race blind is the key variable.

runners_data.name: Thai Baht
runners_data.note: Saffie Osborne partners Owen Burrows' lightly-raced filly who placed over 6f on Soft; style is entirely unknown beyond that single run and she's drawn into a very competitive pace scenario having shown nothing yet on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Polyxena
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani's mount is the only winner in this field, scoring over 6f on Good, and her prominent style fits the predicted race shape precisely; Stuart Williams trains in good form (T14: 4/25) and the 132lb top weight reflects her market prominence.

runners_data.name: Lucky Orla
runners_data.note: Patrick Owens' filly hasn't run in 134 days and faded badly last time at 6f Good — the longest absence in the field combined with the fade flag makes her a significant risk in a race where the pace will expose any fitness deficit.

runners_data.name: Miss Tango
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' filly holds two runs at 6f on Good without threatening the frame; the hold-up style means she needs a pronounced pace implosion to get involved, and her form figures of 7-4 don't scream improvement.

runners_data.name: Nonrem
runners_data.note: Jason Watson on Brian Meehan's filly who has shown consistency without winning in two Good-ground starts; prominent style fits well and the tongue tie (hg:t) may sharpen her up — she's one of the profiles the race shape is designed to suit.

runners_data.name: Plastic Dream
runners_data.note: Chris Dwyer's filly (hg:t) placed fourth on her only start over 6f Good with Silvestre De Sousa retaining the ride — the tongue tie carried over suggests a known issue being managed, and her prominent style puts her right in the firing line tactically.

runners_data.name: Sea Angie Run
runners_data.note: David Egan takes over for Tom Clover but Sea Angie Run's only run was 7th over 7f on Good, a longer trip, and she now drops to 6f as a confirmed pace-setter into a three-way early duel — survival of the early battle is her biggest challenge.

runners_data.name: Sequel Star
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's consistent filly has placed twice (3rd, 4th) over 6f-7f and is one of three confirmed leaders; Ed Walker in strong T14 form (7/40) and Marquand's tactical intelligence mean she's the best-handed of the pace trio to avoid overextending.

runners_data.name: Catalistic
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Rod Millman with no public form and going entirely unknown — impossible to assess pace profile or ground aptitude, and in a field of 15 with a fierce early pace, inexperience is a major exposure.

runners_data.name: Cranberry Breeze
runners_data.note: Another first-time starter for James Keane with zero public evidence on going or style; Ray Dawson takes the ride but there is simply no data upon which to build a tactical case in a race this competitive.

runners_data.name: Decem Carolinae
runners_data.note: Jack Jones' filly ran 6th over 6f on Good 73 days ago and Rossa Ryan is a quality booking; lightly raced flag applies but that debut experience on identical going and trip at least provides a baseline — she's not a complete unknown unlike the other debutants.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Angie Run, Sequel Star, and Romotoso are all confirmed front-runners in a 15-runner field over Windsor's straight 6f, making a strong, contested gallop from the off essentially guaranteed. Sea Angie Run (David Egan) and Romotoso (Oisin Murphy) have the most recognisable early-speed profiles, while Sequel Star (Tom Marquand) has shown consistent place form from prominent positions and will not surrender ground willingly. With three genuine pace-setters fighting for the same real estate, the early fractions will be honest to fast, meaning stamina and the ability to settle just off a strong pace will be at a premium in the closing stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who have the tactical nous to track the pace battle and pick up the pieces — notably Santo, Polyxena, Nonrem, and Plastic Dream — rather than pure front-runners burning energy in an early duel or deep hold-up horses left with too much to do from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way pace battle burns the front-runners out, leaving the prominent-tracking types to swoop
scenarios.body: Sea Angie Run, Romotoso, and Sequel Star cut each other up through the first three furlongs, handing the race to horses who have settled just behind and conserved energy; Polyxena's winning form at 6f on Good and Nonrem's prominent style suit this perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacer Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Romotoso with Oisin Murphy's handling — gains control and isn't pressured as hard as feared
scenarios.body: Murphy manages to ease Romotoso into a comfortable rhythm just ahead of the scrimmage, denying a true pace collapse and sustaining a gallop that suits those who can travel on the bridle; Sequel Star's consistency from near the front also makes it a live player in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that even the prominent runners are cooked, opening a late lane for the deep hold-up horses down the straight
scenarios.body: Miss Tango and Highland Grey, positioned towards the rear, get a dream run through as the field spreads across the track in the closing stages; this shape requires everything to fall right positionally on a straight course, but the violent pace makes a late implosion at least plausible.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Fizzles, Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If two of the three pace-setters miss the break or are eased off early, leaving one uncontested leader
scenarios.body: Without genuine competition for the lead, Sea Angie Run or Sequel Star could soft-pedal the early splits and find reserves to hold on; this scenario requires an uncharacteristic misfire from at least two confirmed speedsters and is the least likely shape given the evidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Oisin Murphy steals a march on Sea Angie Run and Sequel Star at the start on Romotoso — if she breaks fastest and gets a stride's advantage, she may control the pace rather than race in a three-way war.

Polyxena's 132lb top weight is the heaviest in the field and Marco Ghiani must judge the pace perfectly tracking a fierce early gallop — if she gets drawn into racing closer than ideal, her stamina could be tested beyond her form win.

Lucky Orla's 134-day absence combined with a fade flag from her only run makes her a volatile runner to be around in a tight 15-runner field; watch for signs of greenness or lack of peak fitness under Benoit de la Sayette.

With three front-runners drawn across the stalls, watch the draw closely at the off — any front-runner drawn widest will be forced to cross rivals to find position, potentially causing interference and shaking up the early shape.

Catalistic and Cranberry Breeze are complete unknown quantities making their debuts; in a 15-runner field with a strong gallop, watch whether either drifts markedly in the market before post time as a late intelligence signal.

races.name: Matchbook Betting Exchange Supporting Uk Racing Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Alpha Legend
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who fades late (flagged), handles Good ground (2 of 3 runs on similar), but a 83-day absence and a tendency to empty in the finish limits confidence; tongue-tie worn, Marco Botti yard in fair form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with finishes of seventh and two eighths, Alpha Legend heads here 83 days off the track and ranks toward the foot of our figures; experience over today's trip and a return to action are slim pickings for supporters.

runners_data.name: Cruse On Bye
runners_data.note: Won't get the rear berth that suits this hold-up type in a 15-runner field — likely to find itself racing in an unfamiliar midfield role; recent form reads 055 on Good ground and style-fit is discounted at 0.92.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 14 of 15 on our figures, Cruse On Bye faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a fresh enough 15-day break from stall 3 carrying 124 lb.

runners_data.name: So Tempting
runners_data.note: Has a genuine placed run on Good over 6f (2nd most recently on this surface), making her the most interesting of the displaced hold-up types; visor fitted, Tom Ward yard runs two in the race, and she's run four of five on similar ground.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last five starts, So Tempting does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back shows she can threaten; however, the burden of 122 lb from stall 14 may make life harder for a filly rated just 52 officially.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Career best came on Soft (2nd, 5f) and the step up to 6f on Good is an open question; a true closer who won't get to the back of this big field, and the combination of trip/going query and redistribution tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 12 of 15 on our figures, Devon Angel faces a stiff ask here, though a second last time out offers a crumb of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Purple Dream
runners_data.note: Deeply out of form (0600, including 11th and 12th), tendency to fade, and best past effort came on Soft — Good ground is just one of her problems; blinkered, but this hold-up type won't get the ride she needs in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Purple Dream faces a stiff task here; she has run over today's trip before and returns on a quick turnaround of nine days, but there is precious little in the recent form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Blue Skies Above
runners_data.note: 90-day layoff is a significant concern for Tom Marquand's mount; fades in the finish (flagged), best run was a 5th on Good but she's a hold-up horse whose last two runs produced 8th and 10th — hard to be positive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 90 days off, Blue Skies Above faces a stiff task from stall seven carrying 135 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 66 leaves him with a slender edge over his mark.

runners_data.name: Past Passion
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with multiple placed efforts on Good ground (2nd twice, 3rd once) and a strong record at 5f-6f; Jason Watson takes the ride for Jonathan Portman and she's as well-suited as any to stalking a lone front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Past Passion shaped well when second three starts back and third four starts back, and her speed rating of 74 underlines why she heads these rivals on ratings; winless in her last six starts, though, and a trainer firing at just 5% over the past fortnight is the one reservation.

runners_data.name: From Me To You
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose form reads 776040 with no wins; mostly disappoints on Good ground (3/6 similar-going runs) and is blinker-wearing — no compelling reason to override a poor recent profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of unplaced efforts either side of a fourth two starts back, From Me To You heads here nine days after his latest disappointing run, and a trainer firing at just four per cent makes the case harder to press despite carrying 134 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Tallahassee Lassie
runners_data.note: A winner on Good ground over 5f (1W) and has placed twice in similar conditions; Rossa Ryan and James Fanshawe (4/19 T14) represent a sharp combination and her prominent style maps perfectly to this lone front-runner scenario.
runners_data.comment: Tallahassee Lassie won three starts back but has been unplaced in both runs since, and while she has experience over today's trip and going, the recent dip in form is hard to ignore from stall nine carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Wopbopaloomop
runners_data.note: Unknown style flag (U), 114 days off the track — a significant absence — and only three runs, all without a win or place; tongue-tie worn, and Richard Spencer's yard is not firing (2/9 T14).
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and 114 days absent, Wopbopaloomop nonetheless rates 6 lb clear of her official mark and has run over today's trip, making her a live threat from stall one at 131 lb — though recapturing form after that lengthy break is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Lola
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, trained by Tom Ward (2/16 T14), set to get a soft lead on Good ground; form reads 340 with a placing on Good, and the controlled scenario is firmly in her favour if she jumps well.
runners_data.comment: Lola shaped with promise when third three starts back, and at 130 lb from stall two she has fitness on her side returning after 21 days, with experience over today's trip adding quiet confidence; the risk is she has been winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dream On Kent
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two placed efforts on Good ground (2nd twice) and a wide range of trips; Pat Dobbs rides for David Evans (2/20 T14) and this horse is one of the more plausible late-challenge candidates if traffic allows.
runners_data.comment: Dream On Kent carries a significant weight of 129 lb from stall 11, yet his rating of 70 — well clear of his official mark — flags him as a leading danger, and he has run over today's distance and going before; the risk is that he has been winless in his last six starts, with recent form figures trending the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Marralyn
runners_data.note: Naturally races from behind and has a 3rd on Good ground in her record; 44-day break for Ollie Sangster and Stevie Donohoe, and while she's not a standout, she's among the cleaner hold-up types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 11th of 15 on our figures, Marralyn faces a stiff ask here, with a seventh last time out the most recent evidence; a third two starts back offers mild encouragement, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Courage Best
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish (flagged), form reads 7990, and this genuine closer is pushed into a midfield slot it won't naturally occupy; Oisin Murphy's booking is the headline but the style-fit discount (0.92) and poor recent form are hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and returning after 51 days off, Courage Best faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip before and our rating nudges above her official mark — small encouragement for a filly whose recent efforts have been consistently midfield or worse.

runners_data.name: Havananother
runners_data.note: A true rear-of-field type displaced to midfield by the volume of hold-up horses in this race; hood worn, Richard Hughes in fair form (3/26 T14), but the 45-day break and STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 weigh against expectations.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked ninth of fifteen, Havananother faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip before and a 45-day break may have freshened her; 126 lb from stall eight is the neutral hand she's been dealt.

races.paceDynamic: Lola is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner nursery and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Callan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from stall to finish on Good ground at Windsor. Past Passion and Tallahassee Lassie will look to press from prominent positions, giving Lola company through the early stages but not enough to force a truly searching pace. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up horses — Courage Best, Havananother, Cruse On Bye, So Tempting, Devon Angel and Purple Dream are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map because they cannot all get to the rear in a 15-runner sprint, meaning those positions are congested and their chances of executing their natural style are compromised. A controlled front-running tempo on fast-enough Good turf over 6f at Windsor favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort — prominent racers who can travel just off Lola and pounce in the final two furlongs hold the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lola Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lola dictates an honest but sustainable pace and the prominent duo chase her home without serious disruption.
scenarios.body: Lola sets the fractions from the front and the race is run at a gallop that suits those travelling just behind her; Past Passion and Tallahassee Lassie, both proven prominent types with good-ground form, are ideally placed to challenge in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lola Leads, Wins Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely soft enough that Lola's uncontested lead gives her an unassailable advantage turning for home.
scenarios.body: With no horse pressing her hard, Lola is allowed a breather mid-race and simply extends her advantage through the final two furlongs on ground that suits; her Tom Ward stable has been hitting form (T14: 2/16) and this trip and surface are familiar to her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently early to string out the field and a true hold-up horse can find a gap from the redistributed midfield pack.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires one of the genuine closers — So Tempting (2/6f/Good form), Dream On Kent or Marralyn — to find clear running in the final furlong despite being shuffled into a congested midfield rather than their natural rear position; the style-fit discount for the redistributed runners makes this a materially less likely outcome than it might first appear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Wide Draw Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a messy break or mid-race trouble causes bunching and the race becomes a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With 15 runners on a 6f Windsor straight, traffic problems are possible; a horse that can find a clear passage on the outside — Havananother or Devon Angel — could benefit, though both carry style-fit discounts and their redistribution to midfield makes this a low-probability proposition.

watchPoints.text: Lola (Jack Callan) — watch her jump and early stride pattern; if she breaks cleanly and immediately takes her position, the race shape is set and no horse may realistically challenge her for the lead in 15 runners.

Congestion in the first two furlongs — with 15 runners and a large bloc of hold-up horses inevitably shuffled to midfield, jockeys like Oisin Murphy (Courage Best) and Finley Marsh (Havananother) may face traffic problems that effectively end their chances before halfway.

Past Passion and Tallahassee Lassie — watch which of these two prominent types gets the better position at the break; whichever settles cleanest just off Lola's shoulder going into the opening furlong is best placed to challenge in the final stages.

So Tempting (Ashley Lewis, 3lb claim) — the most exposed of the displaced hold-up types on pure form, but if the pace is strong enough to create separation, she's the closer most likely to find the gap; monitor her draw and early position.

Blue Skies Above (Tom Marquand) — a 90-day absence, top jockey booking and the highest weight in the race (135lbs) for an OR-65 horse; if Marquand travels well on the bridle in midfield, she could outrun the layoff, but the fading flag and hold-up style are genuine concerns.

races.name: Follow Matchbook On X Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Great Chieftain
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong similar-going form (14 runs on good, 4 wins) and an excellent record at this trip; Tom Marquand is a meaningful booking and Oliver Cole's T14 strike rate (2/11) is reasonable — the 25-day break is no concern given peak fitness from a busy season.
runners_data.comment: Great Chieftain is the top-rated runner in the field and his speed figure of 86 outstrips his rivals, making him a serious threat despite being winless in his last six starts; the main risk is that his recent form figures give little encouragement, with a sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Ascending Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 8f on good ground recently and has a consistently placed profile (3-3-1-3-3) suggesting reliability; Callum Rodriguez should press forward immediately and the key question is whether Mystic Moment makes this too hot too early.
runners_data.comment: Ascending Star arrives in solid recent nick, third last time out and a winner three starts back, and he handles today's distance and going, with 32 days since his last run suggesting he returns fresh enough to go close from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing type with a course-profile win at 8f on good going and trainer David Evans in strong T14 form (2/20); the 51-day absence is the main concern, though Evans routinely prepares horses well fresh and the form behind the lay-off was solid.
runners_data.comment: Dovey Moon showed what he is capable of with a win four starts back, but has been inconsistent since, finishing third two starts ago before a fifth last time out after 51 days off; he has run over today's trip and going, and carries 137 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Burdett Estate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping significantly back in trip from recent sprint starts (all 5f), stepping up to a mile for the first time; the 107-day absence is the most notable flag in the field, and while Brian Toomey has zero T14 runners, the style suits a contested pace if the trip proves within range.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and absent for over three months, Burdett Estate is hard to fancy at the weights, though he has winning form in recent starts and a third two runs back offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose Saffie Osborne booking keeps costs down; ran a string of consistent placed efforts at 8f on good going, including a win, and the 39-day break looks fine — the race shape, if the front two fight each other, is tailor-made for this profile.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and second three starts back suggests he retains ability, but an unplaced effort last time out and a trainer without a winner in 22 recent attempts are genuine concerns; he has run over today's trip and going, and 39 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with multiple placed efforts at 8f on good going but no wins at this trip; Marco Ghiani picks up rides in form and William Knight's T14 figures (4/12) are encouraging — the consistent near-miss profile makes this a prime pace beneficiary if the front crumbles.
runners_data.comment: Luzon Heights shaped well when third last time out and a second three starts back hints at the quality within his profile, with experience over today's trip and going adding solid grounding; the chief concern is his tendency to find one or two too good, as he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mystic Moment
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner whose recent form (second at 8f on good) shows viable speed; Ashley Lewis takes the 3lb claim which reduces the weight burden, but Neil Mulholland's T14 record (0/9) is a negative flag and the horse has not won since that second, suggesting it may be more useful as a pace-maker than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Mystic Moment steps up as a leading danger, her rating of 85 lending real substance to her claims, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — but winless in her last five starts, the key question is whether that placed effort last time finally sparks a breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Runs on course fresh (10 days), and Jim & Suzi Best's yard has been quietly ticking over; a natural hold-up operator whose last five runs were all over 10f or more, stepping down sharply in trip — pace position is further compressed by the busy front half of this field, and the style-fit discount (0.90) reflects that genuine closers' real estate is scarce here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Golden Circet has shown little sign of breaking that duck, ranking seventh of nine on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and ten days between runs leaves him at least fit to do himself justice.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: In-form three-year-old who has won back-to-back (8f good, 8f soft) and arrives fresh (8 days); John Ryan's T14 record (3/8) is strong and Jack Mitchell is a reliable partner — however, as a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map, securing a genuine rear position in this pace-heavy race will be harder than usual, and the style-fit score (0.92) tempers expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures and with a speed rating just a point below his official mark, Ecclefechan is hard to fancy on ratings, though back-to-back wins in his last two starts and a return just eight days later suggest he arrives in ripe form.

races.paceDynamic: Ascending Star and Mystic Moment are the two confirmed front-runners and will press for the early lead from the jump, creating a genuinely contested pace down the Windsor straight mile from the outset. With both horses likely to push each other through the early fractions, the gallop should be honest rather than suicidal — enough to test stamina reserves but not so frenetic that the race blows itself apart. Great Chieftain and Dovey Moon will look to track closely in the prominent slots just behind the duel, meaning the entire front half of the field is well populated and competitive for position. This race shape most favours hold-up horses who can sit off the pace, conserve energy, and produce a sustained late run — though note that Golden Circet and Ecclefechan, both true hold-up types, have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more deep closers than the rear positions can accommodate, making it most likely that Burdett Estate, Get Outta Here, and Luzon Heights secure the genuine back-of-field spots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Ascending Star and Mystic Moment burn each other off at a genuine clip, setting up a race for horses arriving late.
scenarios.body: The honest early duel drains the front-runners and leaves the race wide open for horses who have settled behind the pace and can sustain their run through the final two furlongs; the Windsor straight mile strongly rewards this profile when pace is genuine.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Ascending Star (or Mystic Moment) gains a comfortable lead and the rival surrenders early, allowing a solo front-runner to control tempo.
scenarios.body: A solo leader controlling a moderate gallop over the Windsor mile can dictate the fractions and use the straight to quicken clear before closers can organise; Ascending Star's recent win at 8f on good ground and stronger trainer form makes this the more likely of the two front-runners to pull it off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is competitive but not punishing and a horse tracking within two lengths of the lead picks its moment perfectly in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Great Chieftain has strong course-equivalent good-ground form and is bred to relish this trip, while Dovey Moon's recent 1m win on good ground confirms the profile; a tracking run from just behind the duel suits both perfectly if the pace is just honest enough but not damaging.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or runners bunch, creating a truly sprint-style finish that rewards the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because Golden Circet and Ecclefechan — the horses whose profile would most suit a pure late-run race — are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to secure their natural rear-of-field position in this pace-heavy field; Ecclefechan has winning form at 8f on good but faces a test of position here.

watchPoints.text: Ascending Star vs Mystic Moment: watch the first two furlongs — if both press hard from the break, the pace could be genuinely punishing and set the race up for closers rather than either front-runner.

Burdett Estate faces a significant trip question stepping from 5f to 1m for the first time after a 107-day absence — watch the market for any move that might indicate confidence the horse has been schooled for this task.

Golden Circet and Ecclefechan are both true hold-up horses in a field where the rear positions are genuinely crowded — watch their early positioning: if they are forced to race mid-division against their instincts, their finishing kicks will be blunted.

Dovey Moon's 51-day break is the longest among the proven good-ground performers at this trip — watch for any signs of ring rustiness in the first half of the race, as David Evans runners often need the run.

Luzon Heights has finished second or third in seven of twelve good-ground runs without winning at 8f — watch whether Ghiani commits earlier than usual given the pace scenario, as a positive ride could turn a place into a win.

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Winter Hill Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Venetian Prince
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's hold-up specialist returns from 80 days off wearing a hood, and his best form at 12f on good ground (1st at 11f on heavy) suggests the trip suits, but he needs the front-runners to genuinely fight to generate the deep closing run he requires.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Prince has been beaten in five of his last six starts, and 80 days off the track does little to inspire confidence for a colt ranked sixth of seven on our figures, though a win two starts back and experience on today's going are minor points in his favour.

runners_data.name: Raaheeb
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows' three-year-old has winning form over 10f on good and brings a clean recent record of 1-1-4 over the trip; Rossa Ryan will look to track the early pace from a prominent position and pounce as the front-runners tire.
runners_data.comment: Dual winner in his last three starts, Raaheeb arrives with experience of today's trip and going and carries 131 lb from stall three; a 71-day absence is the one query, but his rating of 122 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Maho Bay
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's confirmed front-runner has been freshened for 81 days and Buick will look to use early tactical speed to dictate; winning over 10f and 11f suggests the 1m2f trip is within range, though his last two runs show he can be headed late when the pace he sets flatters others.
runners_data.comment: Maho Bay landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and his 128 lb burden after 81 days off is the one question mark over a horse who has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Morris Dancer
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's prominent racer has a fine strike rate in similar going (2 wins, 4 placed from 6 runs on good) but has been campaigned almost exclusively over 7-8f; the step up to 1m2f is the primary unknown and Robert Havlin will need to judge whether the horse stays.
runners_data.comment: Morris Dancer showed smart form when winning three starts back and filling the runner-up spot four starts back, and his going experience is a clear asset; the main concern is a 60-day absence heading into this on the back of a below-par seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: On Message
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up filly is the most recent winner in the field, scoring over 10f on good just 26 days ago, and Saffie Osborne will drop her in from a low draw to deliver a late challenge — she clearly stays the trip well and has five placed efforts at 10f on good going.
runners_data.comment: On Message won last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, arriving here on a workable 26-day break and carrying 125 lb from stall two; the main risk is that two starts back she finished fourth, hinting she can be vulnerable when not quite at her peak.

runners_data.name: Crest Of Fire
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners Jack Channon's front-runner who won last time over 9f on good and has solid placed form; he will contest the lead from the off, but his record of just one win from ten starts on good ground and a tendency to be headed raises questions about whether he can dominate Maho Bay.
runners_data.comment: Crest Of Fire won last time out and was second two starts back, giving him solid recent form, though he has been off 37 days and a rating of 104 ranks him fifth of seven, suggesting he faces stiff company from stall six carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Harmonics
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's prominent type has headgear noted and won over 10f on good at his third-last start; Shane Foley rides, and while his form over the last two runs has been modest, a truly run race at this trip could unlock a renewal of his earlier promise.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and a beaten fifth last time out, Harmonics faces a stiff task at the foot of the field, though he has run over today's trip before and back-to-back wins three and four starts back show he can find the winning thread.

races.paceDynamic: Maho Bay and Crest Of Fire both carry genuine front-running profiles into this seven-runner Group 3, and with William Buick aboard Maho Bay and Tom Marquand on Crest Of Fire, neither handler is likely to concede the lead without a fight — meaning the early gallop will be genuinely contested rather than manufactured. Over 1m2f on good ground at Windsor, two horses pushing for supremacy from the off typically produce an honest, even tempo that stretches the field and exposes those who lack the cruising speed to travel in behind. Raaheeb and Morris Dancer as prominent types will likely slot in just off the pace battle, while the hold-up horses — Venetian Prince and On Message — will be furthest back on a track where finishing positions can be earned by those who stay on strongly from off the pace. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent closers with proven ability to finish powerfully on good ground, as the contested lead should ensure the pace holds all the way to the line and advantage flows to those arriving late with energy in reserve.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Maho Bay and Crest Of Fire genuinely fight for supremacy and burn each other off over the first half-mile, setting a pace that fractures the field.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade honest fractions and fade in the final two furlongs, leaving those who tracked the pace or came from off it with maximum momentum into the straight; on good ground over 1m2f at Windsor, genuine closers who travel smoothly get their ideal canvas.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Crest Of Fire softens the pace early or Maho Bay is restrained, allowing prominent racers to control the contest at a sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: A moderate or steadier gallop means those sitting just behind the leader save energy and kick powerfully in the straight; Morris Dancer and Raaheeb, both prominent types with good Windsor or good-ground form, benefit from this controlled scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If Maho Bay dictates entirely uncontested and Crest Of Fire is outpaced early or settled into a more reserved position by Marquand.
scenarios.body: Buick uses Maho Bay's tactical speed to dictate a deceptively strong but controlled gallop, never allowing the closers to get into a rhythm, and the Appleby runner's stamina over 1m2f proves sufficient to hold on; this outcome demands the second front-runner effectively drops out of the lead battle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early contest between Maho Bay and Crest Of Fire collapses into a crawl through the middle portion before a sprint finish develops.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the field and turns the finish into a test of raw sprint speed rather than stamina, potentially disadvantaging deep closers like Venetian Prince who need a true pace; Harmonics, with top-speed figures over 1m on good ground, could benefit from a dash to the line.

watchPoints.text: Maho Bay and Crest Of Fire — watch the opening two furlongs to see which of Buick or Marquand blinks first; if neither concedes, the pace could be fierce enough to set the race up entirely for late movers.

Morris Dancer — Robert Havlin's horse has never raced beyond 8f and this step to 1m2f is a significant jump; watch how he travels in the middle portion of the race, as any sign of struggling for his position signals the trip is stretching him.

On Message — Saffie Osborne will be furthest back and her window for a run in a small field of seven can close quickly at Windsor; watch whether a clear passage materialises in the straight or whether she gets boxed behind tiring front-runners.

Venetian Prince — the hood is applied here for the first time (noted hg:p flag) and its effect on his behaviour in the early stages is worth monitoring, as hold-up horses who over-race when fresh can compromise the very late run their profile depends on.

Harmonics — Shane Foley crosses from Ireland and the Gosden yard's 14-day record of 8 from 21 is strong; watch if Harmonics is quietly fancied here as a second string to Morris Dancer, particularly if the race develops into a sprint finish.

races.name: G J Colairo Diamond Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Without Prejudice
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden filly who won her sole start over 10f on Good ground — directly relevant form — with William Buick booked and a lightly raced profile that screams long-term potential; the stalking style suits a controlled race shape here and the step to 1m2f looks tailor-made.

runners_data.name: Lissahane Lass
runners_data.note: 130 days off the track, her last two wins came over sprint trips on Tapeta at Southwell and her hold-up style is a poor match for a likely steady-to-fair Windsor gallop; the 1m2f Good turf trip looks untried territory and the absence makes confidence in her current fitness hard to sustain.

runners_data.name: Aura Champagne
runners_data.note: Pat Dobbs and Richard Hannon's filly has been remarkably consistent in placing (three thirds from three starts) and races prominently — she will likely sit just behind Sister Cecilia and is the one most likely to pose an immediate challenge to the leader turning for home on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Saaffya
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Ed Walker, lightly raced and a complete unknown tactically; the going is listed as UNKNOWN for her, which is simply a function of no public data, and George Downing takes the ride — she must be respected as a wildcard but cannot be assessed beyond trainer rep and breeding.

runners_data.name: Yamnah
runners_data.note: Second Gosden debutante in the race alongside Without Prejudice, ridden by Tom Marquand who knows the stable well; the headgear flag (hg:p) suggests a pacifier is fitted, hinting at a potentially exuberant or green temperament, which is worth watching for at the start on a first run over 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Sister Cecilia
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy on the only confirmed front-runner in an 8-runner field means she will get an uncontested lead on Good ground, but she carries a [STYLE_FIT] flag indicating a tendency to fade in the finish — the question is whether the lack of pressure allows her to conserve enough to hold on, or whether a stronger stayer simply reels her in late.

runners_data.name: Stopherandgo
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with an OR of 30 who is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — placed in the midfield of the pace map only because the surplus of closers couldn't all sit at the rear — Kieren Fox faces the task of nursing a veteran hold-up type through a race that isn't expected to be run at the sort of strong gallop he needs; realistic expectations are modest.

runners_data.name: Astrid
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for James Horton and Robert Havlin who is 20 days fresh off a 3rd on Tapeta at Southwell — the switch to Good turf and a longer 1m2f trip introduces unknowns, and her style means she is dependent on a genuinely run race to deliver; form figures of 7-3 suggest ability is there but the race shape may not fall in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Sister Cecilia is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard, will likely stride clear from the gate to control tempo over the 1m2f at Windsor on Good turf — with no genuine challenger for the lead, the pace figures to be honest rather than pressured, creating a smooth, metronomic gallop that keeps the field strung out. Without Prejudice (1 from 1, similar going) and Astrid sit as natural hold-up types who will need the tempo to be genuinely sustained to deliver late, while Aura Champagne will press from a prominent position and represents the most likely immediate threat to Sister Cecilia on the front end. Saaffya and Yamnah are debutantes whose tactical positioning is unknown, adding a wildcard element to the shape. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically be rewarded at Windsor's flat, turning track without a searching gallop — Stopherandgo is a genuine hold-up horse shuffled to the map's midfield because surplus closers cannot all find room, and its chances depend entirely on a pace it is unlikely to receive. This race shape — one uncontested leader, controlled fractions, Good ground — strongly favours a horse with class, stamina, and the ability to quicken from a prominent or stalking position rather than a pure hold-up type reliant on a fast-run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cecilia Controls, Class Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Sister Cecilia bowls along unchallenged and the race is run at a fair, even tempo that fully tests stamina in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sister Cecilia dictates throughout on Good ground and the race becomes a test of class and finishing kick off a genuine but not punishing pace; horses who have tracked in second or third gear benefit most when the final surge begins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is moderate early and a prominent tracker picks off the leader in the final two furlongs with a well-timed effort.
scenarios.body: Aura Champagne or a debutante stalker sits within striking range of Sister Cecilia throughout and produces a sustained run from two out to overhaul the leader; Good ground and no acceleration in the first half suits a horse who can maintain rhythm rather than quicken sharply.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutante Delights
scenarios.trigger: If one of Saaffya or Yamnah — unknown quantities on debut — translates breeding and trainer confidence into an immediate first-time-out win.
scenarios.body: Gosden's Yamnah or Walker's Saaffya, both lightly raced unknowns on debut, settle kindly and produce an uncomplicated forward run over a distance that suits a scopey, unfurnished filly; a Good surface and an uncontested pace gives an inexperienced filly every chance to show raw ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unexpectedly quick or a mid-race surge strings the field out, allowing a hold-up horse to close ground late.
scenarios.body: Astrid or a genuinely staying type closes from rear through beaten horses but Windsor's relatively flat, turning circuit limits the ground that can be made up in the final furlong; Stopherandgo, though mapped to midfield, is a true hold-up horse whose natural style is ill-suited to what this race shape is likely to offer.

watchPoints.text: Sister Cecilia sets the tempo unchallenged but carries a fade flag — watch whether she still has something in reserve entering the final furlong or whether her lead evaporates as stronger stayers hit top gear.

Yamnah wears headgear (pacifier) on debut — watch her behaviour in the stalls and first furlong, as greenness or a slow start from an inexperienced Gosden filly could compromise both her own run and those drawn alongside her.
Lissahane Lass returns after 130 days off the track and has not run over this trip on turf previously — watch her in the paddock for fitness signals before treating any market move as meaningful.

Without Prejudice is the most course-and-distance-relevant horse on paper (1 win from 1 over 10f, Good) and William Buick rarely travels for unimportant rides — watch her position at the halfway point as a guide to whether the race is unfolding to suit her.

Stopherandgo is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped to midfield due to redistribution — if Kieren Fox pushes forward early contrary to the horse's natural style, that is a tactical change worth noting for future reference.

races.name: Bet £20 Get £40 In Free Bets At matchbook.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good 15 days ago under David Egan for Gary & Josh Moore and carries form-proven sim-going credentials, but is a genuine hold-up horse who will be denied its natural position in a field saturated with closers — the redistribution to midfield blunts its finishing power here.
runners_data.comment: Bated Breeze won three starts back and returns in good order on 15 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the danger is that he has been unplaced on his most recent outing and must bounce back under 129 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Pacific Prince
runners_data.note: Drops back to 5f from longer trips, has no wins or places in 11 sim-going runs, and the ⚠ fade flag is a real concern in a race where the tempo may not be fast enough to flatten the leaders — placed wide of its natural rear position, this is a very difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Pacific Prince has been winless in his last six starts — a run that includes a brought-down and three unplaced efforts — and our figures rank him last of twelve in this field, making him very hard to fancy despite the light weight of 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Bama Lama
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who races prominently and fits this pace map genuinely; 66 days off is the key query, but his 5f Good form (placed once in five) and trainer Millman's reasonable strike rate suggest he can be competitive racing close to Call Time throughout.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, all of which have yielded three consecutive sixths, Bama Lama is hard to fancy from stall seven off a 66-day absence, and her ranking of tenth of twelve on our figures makes a turnaround difficult to foresee, despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Tilsworth Ony Ta
runners_data.note: Jenkins runner who has struggled to place in 15 recent runs and wears a tongue tie; a hold-up specialist now forced into midfield by the congestion of closers in this field, and the combination of poor recent form and positional compromise makes a big run hard to envisage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Tilsworth Ony Ta has struggled for consistency throughout recent form, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns from a 63-day break with a clear head.

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a competitive form string (four places from 12 sim-going runs including a 6f Good win) who wears a hood and has Charles Bishop up — a hold-up type with genuine recent ability who could benefit if the pace scenario opens late running lanes.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, My Mate Mackley arrives here just six days after finishing second, with a win three starts back boosting his claims; he has run over today's distance and going, and 135 lb is the one note of caution, though his current form is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this four-year-old mare who wears blinkers and a tongue tie and has an impressive 12 from 15 sim-going record with a win and six places; one of the hold-up types most likely to threaten if the pace compresses, given her strong Good-ground record over 5f.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes over for Carroll and brings a strong sim-going profile (5 from 10, 1W 3P); the 6f-to-5f drop is a small concern but recent form shows a win and place at the trip, and he is a hold-up type with enough pace to be dangerous if the race sets up with a late opening.
runners_data.comment: Washington Heir has shown flashes — a winner and placed efforts sit in his recent record — but his latest run was unplaced and our rating of 48 ranks him ninth of twelve, making him hard to fancy at the weights despite his experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Lethal Blast
runners_data.note: 124 days off for Andy Irvine's nine-year-old who has no recent runs and a modest sim-going record; a hold-up horse whose layoff makes fitness the overriding concern and who needs everything to go right late in the race.
runners_data.comment: Lethal Blast arrives 124 days on from her last outing and is yet to win in recent starts, though a third three starts back shows she can get involved; the 132 lb burden from stall 12 adds to her task.

runners_data.name: Cabeza De Llave
runners_data.note: Attwater's seven-year-old has shown consistent mid-range form over 5f Good (11 from 15 sim-going, 0W 5P) and is a hold-up type by nature; jockey Paddy Bradley faces the challenge that this horse's natural rear position is unavailable in this crowded closer-heavy field.
runners_data.comment: Cabeza De Llave shapes as the chief threat on ratings, our figure of 57 ranking him top of the twelve, and he has experience of today's distance and going; the concern is a winless recent run of six starts, and 48 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Call Time
runners_data.note: The one genuine front-runner in the race, Pat Dobbs rides for J S Moore who has two winners from 17 in the 14-day window; wears a hood and has a fair 2-from-15 sim-going record — the pace map belongs to this horse and it sets the tactical terms for everyone else.
runners_data.comment: Call Time is winless in his last five starts, though a third two runs back offers a crumb of encouragement; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, but returning just five days after his latest fifth leaves freshness a concern.

runners_data.name: Reporter
runners_data.note: Hodgson's four-year-old has one win from 15 sim-going outings but recent form reads poorly (-60760) and he is a hold-up specialist displaced into midfield by the sheer volume of closers — without a clear rear berth, the finishing kick that produced that single win is harder to replicate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Reporter at least returns on a quick enough turnaround at 21 days and has experience over today's trip and conditions, though a string of sixth-place finishes and unplaced efforts make improvement hard to fancy at a mark of 47.

runners_data.name: Roman Spring
runners_data.note: O'Neill rides this six-year-old for Cook & Bridger who has three places from eight Good-ground runs; a genuine prominent type who legitimately belongs near the front of this pace map alongside Call Time and Bama Lama, making this one of the few horses for whom the drawn position and style align cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Roman Spring has been placed twice in his last six starts — second last time out and third six starts back — yet remains winless, and at 129 lb from stall 3 he carries weight that will test his resolution, though experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Call Time is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only Bama Lama and Roman Spring as genuine prominent types to apply any pressure, is highly likely to bowl along in front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this straight 5f at Windsor. The pace will be honest rather than frenetic — Good ground and a clear lead for Call Time means the fractions are unlikely to be extreme in either direction, keeping the rail-hugging leaders in contention deep into the closing stages. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers and those who can travel just off the pace, as the lack of a contested early duel removes the late finishing surge that true hold-up horses depend upon. The field contains a significant surplus of hold-up types — Bated Breeze, Cabeza De Llave, Reporter, Tilsworth Ony Ta and Pacific Prince are all genuine closers who are unable to get to the rear in the way they need, meaning several will be shuffled into unnatural midfield positions and are unlikely to finish with their usual effectiveness.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rails Win
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time leads uncontested at a steady-to-fair gallop and the pace never truly quickens into a sprint.
scenarios.body: Call Time dictates from the front on Good turf with Bama Lama and Roman Spring tucked in close, and the race is run at a tempo that rewards positional runners who can sustain effort over the final furlong rather than those needing a late burst. Horses racing prominently or just off the leader will have first run and the widest margin of comfort.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Bama Lama or Roman Spring challenge Call Time early and the trio race in a tight group throughout.
scenarios.body: A moderate three-way contest develops at the front with Good ground keeping the pace honest, and the winner emerges from those three horses racing in the first two lengths — no hold-up horse gets close enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Off Modest Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time crawls and the field compresses into a bunched finish, giving hold-up horses an unexpected chance.
scenarios.body: A very slow early pace drags the entire field tight together and the closer runners, particularly Dreambird Dolly or Washington Heir who have proven Good-ground form and tactical discipline, suddenly find themselves in contention entering the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Call Time burns out after leading too freely and the entire front group fades in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: An atypically strong early gallop exhausts the leaders and a hold-up runner who has tracked wide and found clear air — most plausibly Cabeza De Llave or My Mate Mackley — picks up the pieces from a midfield position.

watchPoints.text: Call Time has the entire pace map to itself — if Pat Dobbs controls the tempo and is never pressured, this horse's map dominance could be the decisive tactical edge and any drifting of its price deserves attention.

Roman Spring and Bama Lama are the only other genuine prominent types; if either breaks poorly or is slow away, the three-way front group collapses to one and Call Time's advantage becomes almost unassailable.

Dreambird Dolly's 12-from-15 sim-going record is the standout statistical angle among the hold-up runners — if any late-running scenario materialises, she is best-placed to exploit it and underestimation is a risk.

Several hold-up horses (Bated Breeze, Cabeza De Llave, Reporter, Tilsworth Ony Ta, Pacific Prince) are all forced into midfield positions they do not naturally occupy — watch for crowding and interference between the 2f and 1f poles as these horses attempt to find gaps simultaneously.

Lethal Blast returns after 124 days absent with no recent racecourse evidence of fitness — any dramatic market move for Andy Irvine's nine-year-old would be a meaningful signal worth noting before the off.
